uncited: It solves the bottleneck where standard rasterization overestimates Gaussian extents, processes non-intersecting pixels, and suffers from serial blending latency [Child](3543-speedy-splat-rendering-pipeline.md).

What sets this family apart from sibling methods like [3D Gaussian Splatting Differentiable Rasterizer](2813-3d-gaussian-splatting-differentiable-rasterizer.md) (which focuses on the differentiable math) or [3D Gaussian Splatting MVP](3410-3d-gaussian-splatting-mvp.md) (which focuses on memory layout) is the explicit restructuring of the rendering pipeline stages—specifically moving culling to parallel preprocess phases, replacing coarse bounding-box tests with precise geometric checks, and co-designing hardware units for projection and sorting [Child](3543-speedy-splat-rendering-pipeline.md)[Child](7329-hardware-accelerated-gaussian-rasterization.md)[Child](8365-adr-gaussian.md).

All methods in this family operate on the standard tile-based rasterization model for 3DGS, where the image is divided into fixed-size tiles (typically $16 \times 16$ pixels) [Child](3543-speedy-splat-rendering-pipeline.md)[Child](7329-hardware-accelerated-gaussian-rasterization.md)[Child](8365-adr-gaussian.md).
**Early Culling:** Moving the determination of Gaussian-tile intersection from the serial render stage to the parallel preprocess stage.
This prevents the allocation of memory and processing time for Gaussians that do not contribute to the final image [Child](8365-adr-gaussian.md).

**Precise Intersection:** Replacing the coarse Axis-Aligned Bounding Box (AABB) test of the projected 2D covariance ellipse with precise geometric checks (e.g., ellipse-AABB intersection or adaptive radius bounding circles) to minimize false positives [Child](8365-adr-gaussian.md).

**Depth Sorting:** Maintaining a depth-sorted list of Gaussians per tile to enable correct front-to-back alpha compositing, often using hardware-accelerated or radix-sort based approaches [Child](3543-speedy-splat-rendering-pipeline.md)[Child](7329-hardware-accelerated-gaussian-rasterization.md).
where $\mathcal{N}$ is the set of surviving Gaussians in the tile, sorted by depth [Child](7329-hardware-accelerated-gaussian-rasterization.md).
where $\sigma_i$ is the Gaussian opacity and $g_i(p)$ is the projected 2D Gaussian value at pixel $p$ [Child](7329-hardware-accelerated-gaussian-rasterization.md).
